Front: Classpath vs module path, and what does it mean that your class is in the "unnamed module"?
Back: The classpath is the list of directories and JARs where the JVM looks for classes and resources. The module path is JPMS: named modules with `module-info.java`, where `requires` declares a dependency and `exports` exposes a package. Code loaded from the classpath belongs to the unnamed module: `MyClass.class.getModule().getName()` returns null. It reads every module but has no explicit boundaries.

Front: Why can code compile and then fail with NoClassDefFoundError, and what's the difference between `java -cp` and `java -jar`?
Back: A class available at compile time can be missing from the runtime classpath (dependency not packaged, wrong -cp). `java -cp app.jar com.x.Main` uses the given classpath and you name the main class. `java -jar app.jar` reads Main-Class (and Class-Path) from META-INF/MANIFEST.MF and ignores -cp; a plain JAR without Main-Class fails with "no main manifest attribute".

Front: What's inside a Spring Boot executable JAR, and Main-Class vs Start-Class?
Back: BOOT-INF/classes holds your application classes and resources; BOOT-INF/lib holds dependency JARs (embedded Tomcat, Jackson, Spring) as nested JARs; META-INF/MANIFEST.MF has the metadata. The JDK can't load nested JARs, so Main-Class points to Spring Boot's launcher (JarLauncher), which builds the classpath and calls Start-Class, your @SpringBootApplication main. Maven is build-time only: the JAR runs anywhere with a compatible JRE via `java -jar`, configured per environment (e.g. --server.port=9090).
